claims.text: The starting alloy is W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The starting alloy was produced by magnetron sputtering.
The starting alloy is nanocrystalline with a grain size near 70 nm.
The starting alloy has a metastable BCC structure.
Increasing V above 11 at.% will suppress radiation-induced precipitation.
Increasing V above 11 at.% will allow the alloy to retain negligible irradiation hardening.
Increasing V above 11 at.% will facilitate practical bulk processing.
Additional V will enhance chemical short-range order and produce a more homogeneous BCC solid solution.
Additional V will refine the grain structure.
Additional V will balance vacancy and self-interstitial mobilities.
Additional V reduces self-interstitial mobility relative to the other alloy constituents.
Bringing vacancy and interstitial mobilities closer together enhances defect recombination.
Enhanced defect recombination minimizes the accumulation of large interstitial clusters.
Large interstitial clusters leave excess vacancies that drive precipitation.
Additional V weakens ordering or segregation tendencies and thereby suppresses radiation-induced elemental segregation at grain boundaries.
At approximately 1073 K and 8 dpa, the V-enriched alloy will have a lower precipitate volume fraction and smaller precipitates than the unmodified alloy.
At approximately 1073 K and 8 dpa, the V-enriched alloy will maintain a stable nanocrystalline BCC morphology.
Under similar irradiation conditions, unmodified W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits measurable radiation-induced precipitation.
Under similar irradiation conditions, unmodified W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits minor irradiation hardening.
The proposed beneficial effects are applicable around 1073 K and up to approximately 8 dpa in nanocrystalline sputtered films.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator invokes enhanced V-dependent chemical short-range order, whereas the mechanism invokes a weakened ordering tendency. The hypothesis does not distinguish beneficial short-range order from the ordering that is supposedly weakened.
